reasoning: The wheat heads show complete replacement of grain/spikelet tissue with dark brown-black powdery spore masses that are partially dispersed, leaving the rachis intact. This is the classic presentation of Loose Smut (Ustilago tritici), where the entire head is converted to teliospores that disperse at heading time. Leaves and stems appear healthy, ruling out foliar diseases. The pattern is inconsistent with Head Scab (which shows bleached spikelets), Dwarf Bunt (individual bunt balls), or rust diseases (pustules on leaves/stems).
